finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it. An attacker can set privileged or identity fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email, passwordHash, tenant/org id) on their own account, leading to privilege escalation or account takeover.

trace.note: Object.assign merges all body keys into req.user with no allowlist
req.store.save persists the modified user, including privileged fields
Full user object is returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation in this file. The sibling route PUT /me/profile (line 11) destructures only displayName and bio, which shows the intended restriction is missing here. Authentication middleware that populates req.user is not in the repo (only users.js exists), so it was not checked and is assumed. Could not confirm whether req.store.save filters fields.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, users.js:6 persists it and users.js:7 returns it, while the sibling route at users.js:11 destructures only displayName and bio, so any authenticated user can overwrite their own privileged fields (the auth middleware and store.save are not in the repo, so field filtering there is unconfirmed).
